cards.front: The three delirium subtypes are hyperactive (agitation, hallucinations), [___] (lethargy, reduced awareness — most commonly missed, worst prognosis), and mixed (fluctuates between both).
cards.context:
Ward staff describe these patients as 'settled' or 'sleeping well,' while in reality they are profoundly confused with ongoing organ dysfunction.

Studies show hypoactive delirium is missed in up to 70% of cases without systematic screening (e.g., CAM or 4AT).

cards.front: [___] competence allows a minor to consent to treatment if they demonstrate sufficient understanding and maturity, assessed on a case-by-case basis rather than by a fixed age.
cards.context: Gillick competence (from the 1986 UK case Gillick v West Norfolk) establishes that capacity is assessed individually, not by a fixed age threshold.

cards.front: Buprenorphine is preferred over methadone in patients with [___] prolongation because it has minimal cardiac conduction effects.
cards.context: Buprenorphine has minimal effect on the hERG potassium channel and does not prolong the QTc interval, unlike methadone which can cause torsades de pointes.

cards.front: New-onset visual hallucinations in a hospitalised patient are [___] until proven otherwise.
cards.context: Visual hallucinations in the medical setting are a red flag for organic pathology rather than primary psychosis.

cards.front: Key family systems concepts in child psychiatry include enmeshment vs disengagement, [___] (a child drawn into parental conflict to stabilise the dyad), and parentification (child forced into adult caretaking role).
cards.context:
These concepts help explain why a child's symptoms may be maintained by family dynamics rather than individual pathology.

Triangulation occurs when a dyadic conflict pulls in a third person (often a child) to stabilise the relationship. Parentification forces a child into an adult caretaking role, disrupting normal development.

Recognising these patterns changes the treatment target from the child alone to the family system.
